body.p: Entry of the above amendments is requested. The amendments to claim 1, 9 and 17 are supported by, for example, paragraph [0065] and Figures 7 and 8. The amendments to claims 2, 4, 6-8, 10, 12, 14-16, 18-19, 21, 23, 25 and 27-29 recite language removed from claims 1, 9 and 17. No new matter has been added. Claims 1-29 are pending.
Claims 1 - 29 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. 2017/0164878 to Connor et al and U.S. 2021/0244308 to Bosua. Applicant traverses the rejections.

With respect to claim 1, the combination of Connor and Bosua does not teach or suggest a non-invasive analyte sensor where in the first group the first side edge of one of the two antennas faces the second side edge of the other of the two antennas in the first group, and the first side edge of an antenna in the first group faces the second side edge of an antenna in the second group.

With respect to claim 9, the combination of Connor and Bosua does not teach or suggest a non-invasive analyte sensor where in the first group a first side edge of one of the two antennas faces a second side edge of the other of the two antennas in the first group; and the first side edge of an antenna in the first group faces a second side edge of an antenna in the second group.

With respect to claim 17, the combination of Connor and Bosua does not teach or suggest a non-invasive analyte sensor where a side edge of a first one of the antennas faces a side edge of a second one of the antennas, and another side edge of the second one of the antennas faces a side edge of a third one of the antennas.

The rejection references Figure 61 and paragraphs [0721]-[0722] of Connor as being relevant to claims 1, 9 and 17. However, Figure 61 of Connor and Bosua do not teach or suggest the features now recited in claims 1, 9 and 17.

An annotated version of Figure 61 of Connor is reproduced below. Figure 61 of Connor discloses sensor units spaced along a circumferential band, with each sensor unit including a transmit antenna (indicated by the + sign) and a receive antenna (indicated by the - sign). See paragraph [0632]. The exact shapes and orientations of the transmit

antennas and the receive antennas is not disclosed in Connor. Figures 3B-D of Bosua teach arranging two antennas side-by-side with one another, while Figure 9 of Bosua teaches an antenna array with three antennas arranged side-by-side with equal spacing between the antennas.
As indicated in the annotated version of Connor Figure 61 below, based on the
teachings of Bosua, the transmit and receive antennas in each sensor unit of Connor could be arranged side-by-side as indicated below.
annotated figure above, there would only be two antennas arranged side-by-side, or at best three antennas arranged side-by-side with equal spacing between the antennas as taught in Figure 9 of Bosua.
Connor and Bosua, singly and in combination, do not teach or suggest an
arrangement with three or four antennas that are arranged, oriented and spaced from one another, with the facing side edges, as recited in claims 1, 9 and 17.
For at least these reasons, claims 1, 9 and 17 are patentable over Connor and

Bosua. Claims 2-8, 10-16 and 18-29 depend from claims 1, 9 and 17 respectively, and are patentable therewith for that reason alone and need not be separately distinguished at this time. Applicant does not concede the rejections to the dependent claims.
Favorable reconsideration in the form of a notice of allowance is requested. Any questions concerning this paper can be directed to the attention of the undersigned at (612) 371-5349.
